faq.q: What does a before and after product video show?
faq.a: Keep your product in frame and show the starting state, the change, and the final result in one short ad.

faq.q: How do I make a before and after video from one photo?
faq.a: Upload the before photo and describe the after in a sentence. Read the line when the file comes back, then change the music before you export.

faq.q: Which products fit a before and after video?
faq.a: Shops with a change people can see, such as a surface getting clean or a texture getting smooth. TikTok can take a tall file, and a feed can take a square.

faq.q: What does a before and after clip cost?
faq.a: Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A 6-second clip is 24 credits, 10 seconds is 40, 15 is 60, and 30 is 120. You see the number before it starts. If the video fails, the credits come back.

faq.q: Can the file run as an ad I paid for?
faq.a: Yes. Commercial use is part of a paid plan, and the download has no watermark. You still need rights to the photo you uploaded.

faq.q: Which video shapes can I download?
faq.a: You can download 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4. Use the tall file for TikTok, the square for a feed, or the wide file for a landscape placement.

faq.q: Can every product in the catalog get a clip?
faq.a: Yes. Send a photo for each product, and you get a separate clip for each. Store software can request them through the API.

faq.q: Can an AI avatar narrate the change?
faq.a: Yes. Pick an AI avatar to narrate the change. Keep a filmed piece when a flagship spot needs your own camera.

faq.q: Could TikTok or Meta turn the ad down?
faq.a: Maybe. Read TikTok and Meta rules before you spend. Add a label if a viewer might think a real buyer is reviewing the product. The person on screen is an AI actor.

reviews.h2: How Shops Show One Product Change
reviews.lead: Four sellers start from a photo they already own. Each clip keeps the same product and changes one visible thing.

items.d: A home cleaner shop uploads one greasy stovetop and shows that same stove wiped clean. They post the clip on the product page and skip booking the kitchen twice.
A cream seller shows one hand, dry on one side and with cream on the other, and the jar stays in frame. They use the clip in a paid social ad and skip hiring a hand model.

A knitwear shop shows pills on one half of a camel sweater and a smooth knit on the other, with the fabric shaver in frame. They send the tall file to a phone feed and skip a second day of laying the sweater flat.
A kitchen shop shows whole garlic on one half of a wood board and pressed garlic on the other. They download the square for a feed ad and skip resetting the board for a second take.
